request: How does Bayesian optimization decide which setting to try next?

composition.story: Why might a lower prediction earn the next trial? Review completed trials, then inspect Settings A and B. This fixed, noiseless example maximizes score using expected improvement: average positive gain above the best observed score. Gaussian predictions are supplied, not fitted here. Use Next; the decision remains visible until you act.

aha.observation: Setting B wins because its uncertainty creates more expected improvement, despite its lower predicted score.

parts.presentation: Place below the explanation and above the experiment. Highlight the active state; keep all progress on this rail. Steps represent decisions, not elapsed time.
Use one fixed row with three named regions. Only the active region changes highlight. Keep labels readable without motion or a matrix.
Anchor beside the active region without covering labels. Identify the setting and explain its role; report numerical values only in readouts.

Show one active-setting evidence stack, not a candidate matrix. Scores, uncertainty, and expected improvement share score-point units. Uncertainty denotes one standard deviation. Expected improvement is computed from each Gaussian forecast against the same observed best. Round displayed numbers to two decimals. Keep the observed-best readout anchored. Use the final entry as the bound status line.

controls.label: Decision step
controls.presentation: Parameter-control budget: zero; navigation and reset are separate. Provide Previous and Next, moving exactly one state per action. Default to the first state; bounds are the first and last states. Retain button names when disabled at boundaries. Every state persists until another action; never advance automatically. Use visible keyboard focus and native keyboard activation.

controls.label: Reset
controls.presentation: Restore the first state and all defaults. Provide visible focus and keyboard activation. Reference captures must show the named aha state.

variants.label: Expected improvement with fixed Gaussian forecasts

states.label: Observed best
states.sentence: Completed trials establish the result to beat.
states.why: Expected improvement counts only gains above this baseline; worse outcomes contribute zero improvement.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Compare the two untried settings next.

states.label: Inspect A
states.sentence: Setting A predicts a modest, fairly certain improvement.
states.why: Its narrow uncertainty keeps most possible outcomes close to its predicted score.

states.label: Choose next
states.sentence: Setting B is the next trial.
states.why: Its wider uncertainty offers enough upside to outweigh its lower predicted score.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Choose B: highest expected improvement among these candidates.
